cards.title: Reference water demand is not an irrigation depth
principles: ET0 describes atmospheric evaporative demand for a reference surface and is driven by weather.
Crop water use requires crop and growth-stage information, commonly represented by a crop coefficient, in addition to ET0.
A rain-minus-ET0 value is a useful weather-pressure indicator, but it is not the irrigation depth to apply.
guardrails: Do not convert forecast ET0 or rain-minus-ET0 directly into an irrigation amount when crop coefficient, effective rainfall, soil storage, rooting depth, and application efficiency are unavailable.

sources.title: Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements

cards.title: Irrigation timing depends on the root-zone water balance
principles: The crop root zone acts as a water reservoir that is depleted by crop water use and replenished by effective rain and irrigation.
Crop stress becomes more likely after root-zone depletion exceeds the readily available water threshold.
Rooting depth, soil water-holding capacity, crop sensitivity, runoff, drainage, and irrigation efficiency affect a field schedule.
guardrails: Without field soil moisture or a calibrated root-zone balance, recommend field checking and prioritization rather than an exact irrigation date or volume.

sources.title: FAO-56 Chapter 8: ETc under soil water stress conditions

cards.title: NDVI is strongest as a temporal vegetation indicator
principles: NDVI is an indicator of vegetation greenness, density, and condition, not a direct measurement of irrigation.
Comparison with the same part of prior seasons helps separate unusual behavior from normal crop development.
NDVI can saturate over dense vegetation and can be influenced by soil background and phenological stage.
guardrails: Do not label a cause such as water shortage from NDVI alone; combine it with moisture indices, weather, temporal change, crop context, and spatial persistence.

sources.title: NDVI, the foundation for remote-sensing phenology

cards.title: NDMI indicates changes in canopy water content
principles: NDMI combines near-infrared and shortwave-infrared reflectance to track changes related to vegetation liquid water content.
A declining NDMI can support a drying interpretation when it agrees with the crop's own history, weather, and neighboring cells.
Canopy moisture response can lag or be influenced by crop development, harvest, disease, soil exposure, and mixed land cover.
guardrails: NDMI does not prove that irrigation occurred or did not occur, and it does not replace soil-moisture observations.

sources.title: NDWI: A normalized difference water index for remote sensing of vegetation liquid water

cards.title: Optical EO evidence must respect clouds, resolution, and mixed pixels
principles: Sentinel-2 Level-2A provides scene classes for cloud, cloud shadow, vegetation, bare soil, water, snow, and invalid observations.
The source bands used by vegetation and moisture indices have 10 m or 20 m pixel spacing, while this system summarizes evidence to 250 m cells.
Cell aggregation stabilizes an area-level signal but can hide within-cell variability and mixed land cover.
guardrails: Treat isolated jumps and boundary cells cautiously; repeated behavior across nearby cells and weeks is more operationally meaningful.

cards.title: A seven-day forecast is a scenario, not an observation
principles: Forecast rainfall and ET0 can change which already-stressed areas should be checked first.
Forecast uncertainty should be represented in decisions through conditional language and adjustable actions.
Current observations and model priority remain separate from the future weather scenario.
guardrails: Use phrases such as 'if the forecast holds' and avoid presenting a forecast as a confirmed irrigation need.

sources.title: Communicating forecast uncertainty for service providers

cards.title: Repeated zones are stronger evidence than isolated cells
principles: A coherent cluster of neighboring high-priority cells is more useful for field operations than an isolated cell with the same score.
Persistence or worsening across consecutive observations strengthens the case for field inspection.
A single-week change can reflect phenology, observation conditions, or local management and should be checked against history.
guardrails: Do not invent persistence when only one observation is supplied.

cards.title: Echmiadzin public decision contract
principles: WAIT, SOON, and NOW are rule-based priority classes from 2-week NDMI level and trend, the cell's own history, and recent rain; AI explains them but does not replace or relabel them.
NOW requires dry conditions in two consecutive weeks; the next-week forecast is a model estimate of next week's class, not an observation.
NOW means high irrigation priority and a reason to inspect or coordinate, not an automatic instruction to irrigate.
Crop type is a stable system estimate derived from historical seasonal behavior and is contextual evidence, not ground truth.
guardrails: Do not expose internal validation labels, hidden-cell reasons, API details, or unsupported certainty statements in public text.
